summary: Microsoft's AI-oriented quant investment platform for researching, backtesting and deploying machine learning trading strategies.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Qlib is an open-source quantitative investment platform from Microsoft that applies machine learning to finance. It covers the whole research loop: preparing market data, training models, backtesting strategies and evaluating results.
sixtySeconds.problem: Building a quant research pipeline means stitching together data handling, models, backtests and reports. Qlib provides those pieces and a qrun tool that runs a full workflow from one config file.
whoFor: Data scientists exploring ML for finance
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a complete, research-grade ML quant platform with benchmark workflows, from Microsoft.
requirements: Market data (see the data preparation section)

overview: Install with pip install pyqlib for the latest stable release, or from source for the newest features. The README recommends conda, since installing outside conda can miss header files.

You need data before running workflows. The official dataset is temporarily disabled, and the README points to a community data source you can download into ~/.qlib/qlib_data/cn_data. The qrun tool then builds the dataset, trains a model, backtests and evaluates in one go.
The README warns of an unreleased breaking change for source builds that restricts loading saved artifacts. Qlib is MIT licensed.

steps.title: Download data
steps.body: The official dataset is temporarily disabled; the README suggests this community source.
steps.code:
wget https://github.com/chenditc/investment_data/releases/latest/download/qlib_bin.tar.gz
mkdir -p ~/.qlib/qlib_data/cn_data
tar -zxvf qlib_bin.tar.gz -C ~/.qlib/qlib_data/cn_data --strip-components=1
rm -f qlib_bin.tar.gz
